derivedFrom.revisedAgainstSpecs: The ledger classification was the starting point, not the authority. Every row was re-derived from the milestone spec, required experiments and validation matrix in docs/milestones.json and docs/milestones/*/VALIDATION.md, plus docs/VALIDATION-PLAN.md, and then every row of every surface was swept a second time rather than only the rows a reviewer named. Eleven rows moved off the ledger's answer: M0-AC06 and M0-AC09 to config-experiment, M0-AC01 to bootstrap, M0-AC10 to repo-settings, M1-AC09 to installed, M2-AC12 and M6-AC09 to benchmark, M3-AC10 and M6-AC06 to accessory, M5-AC09 to gui, M6-AC11 to per-claim. The four rows left on config -- M0-AC02, M0-AC05, M1-AC12, M6-AC13 -- were each re-read against their matrix row and kept: every one of them is a claim about committed files or about the run of the pull request under review. The ledger is a dated account of one run and is not rewritten to match. The level A rows were then swept twice more by executor; see executorSplit and macosExecutorSplit.
derivedFrom.portableJob: The executorSplit ended by naming the fix for the gap it surfaced -- run the portable suite unconditionally -- and leaving it to its own slice. That slice added the portable-ubuntu-arm64 job to .github/workflows/ci.yml: no `if:`, no `needs:` and no scope gate, running `swift test --package-path Packages/LabelCore` and scripts/run-accelerator-checks.py on the Linux runner on every pull request and push, with ci-required accepting only `success` from it. automated-swift therefore moves from selected-pull-requests to every-pull-request and drops its reachedWhen. Its twenty-three rows did not move and neither did its level: this changes which pull requests obtain a pass, not what a pass establishes. Two limits are recorded rather than rounded away. The portable job runs the debug configuration only; the release-configuration pass stays inside scripts/ci-swift.sh in the gated macOS job, so a pull request that does not select that job obtains no release-configuration result for these rows. And automated-macos did not move: its executors are Packages/LabelMac and a Darwin-gated shell script, which the Linux job does not and cannot run. The counts become 31 every-pull-request, 10 selected and 49 separate, which are counts of places a pass can be obtained and not of criteria satisfied.
derivedFrom.macosExecutorSplit: A third sweep asked of every level A row the question the executor split had asked of `automated` -- which program produces this row's evidence, and where can that program run -- and found two answers the executor split had missed. (1) M5-AC12 sat on automated-preflight because scripts/check_native_artifacts.py, a Python module with tests in scripts/tests, carries signing-mode rules. That module is the checker, not the executor: it validates captures, and its Python tests exercise synthetic ones. The signing-mode default and the Developer-ID refusal are owned by scripts/build-local-app.sh lines 5-22, which exits 2 unless `uname -s` is Darwin, and that script is invoked from exactly one place -- scripts/ci-swift.sh lines 87 and 91 -- inside the gated macOS job. An earlier claim that no Swift implementation of this rule exists was checked with a grep for SigningMode, signingMode, local-ad-hoc and adHoc across Packages/*/Sources and Packages/*/Tests, which returns nothing: a correct answer to the wrong question, because the executor is bash. (2) M2-AC05 binds OfflineRenderWorkerTests, OfflineExtractionWorkerTests and WorkerBitmapBindingTests, and M3-AC03 binds ProfileBoundFinishingJobPlanTests, in docs/ACCEPTANCE-EVIDENCE.json; all four files are under Packages/LabelMac, which does not build on Linux, and `xcrun swift test --package-path Packages/LabelMac` appears only at scripts/ci-swift.sh lines 66-67. automated-swift describes the portable engine, so directing an agent there for these rows named a session that cannot produce their pass. Every live record in docs/ACCEPTANCE-EVIDENCE.json was checked for LabelMac citations, not only the two named: M2-AC04 and M2-AC13 cite LabelCore paths only and stay on automated-swift. Both cases take one surface, automated-macos, because both give the same answer to the question a surface asks: the pass is obtained by scripts/ci-swift.sh on an Apple Silicon macOS host, and in CI only in swift-macos-arm64, gated on the same swift_changed output. It is kept apart from automated-swift because those rows can also be obtained in a portable Linux session and these cannot, and apart from macos-native because a surface must declare the level its criteria prescribe: these three are prescribed A and the macos-native rows are prescribed I. The four rows left on automated-preflight -- M0-AC07, M0-AC08, M0-AC11 and M6-AC01 -- were each re-derived the same way and each one's executor is a Python checker the always-running job runs, so none of them moved.
derivedFrom.executorSplit: The `automated` surface claimed every-pull-request reach on the reasoning that its portable tests run in the Linux container on any branch whatever the diff contains. That is true of a local run and false of CI, which is what this map publishes. In .github/workflows/ci.yml the always-running repository-preflight job runs exactly scripts/check_repo.py, `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`, scripts/evidence_currency.py, scripts/manifest_audit.py and scripts/ci_scope.py. `swift test --package-path Packages/LabelCore` and scripts/run-accelerator-checks.py appear only in scripts/ci-swift.sh, which only the swift-macos-arm64 job runs, and that job is gated on swift_changed. A documentation-only pull request therefore exercised no Swift-backed A-level row at all while the map said it exercised thirty. So `automated` is split by what actually produces each row's evidence. automated-preflight keeps every-pull-request and holds the four rows the Python checkers and the scripts/tests suite decide: M0-AC07 (action pinning and workflow configuration, check_repo.py), M0-AC08 (links, JSON, milestone documents and progress consistency, check_repo.py), M0-AC11 (docs/reference-target.json validated by check_reference_target.py with scripts/tests/test_reference_target.py, plus the Package.swift minimum and runner assertions check_repo.py makes by reading those manifests as text rather than building them) and M6-AC01 (the requirement-to-evidence mapping check_repo.py and traceability_report.py build, covered by scripts/tests/test_traceability_report.py and evidence_currency.py). Each of those four was re-derived by naming the program that produces its evidence rather than by grepping for a language, and each one is a Python checker the Linux preflight job runs; none is produced by any of the three Darwin-gated shell scripts -- scripts/build-local-app.sh, scripts/host-preflight.sh and scripts/sign-local-diagnostic.sh -- which scripts/ci-swift.sh alone invokes. automated-swift takes twenty-three, whose evidence is produced by the portable LabelCore Swift suite or by run-accelerator-checks.py: M0-AC03, which is the LabelCore build and test run itself; the eight remaining M2 rows, whose geometry, layout, preview, band, compression, ordering and resource-limit vectors are Swift tests and, for M2-AC13, the label-core-lab vectors the independent oracle verifies; the six remaining M3 rows, whose capability, settings, control-mapping, persistence, transport, privacy and profile rules are Swift types and tests; the eight M4 rows, whose extraction geometry, ordering, mismatch and import rules are likewise Swift; and their level is unchanged, because a level says what a pass establishes and this split changes only which pull requests obtain one. Where a row cites both executors, as M2-AC13 does, it takes automated-swift: the claim a Python test cannot make on its own decides the row. This is a real gap in CI coverage that the map surfaced, not a labelling error; closing it by running the portable suite unconditionally is a change to .github/workflows/ci.yml and belongs in its own slice. A later sweep moved three level A rows off these two surfaces onto automated-macos; see macosExecutorSplit.

note: Two questions, not one. A surface answers where a pass can be obtained; `reach` answers which pull requests get there. Conflating them was wrong in every direction. Criteria whose evidence is repository and CI inspection but which need purpose-built pull requests were counted as reachable; criteria at level I whose prescribed measurement is a named local machine were counted as hosted CI; and a boolean could not say that hosted macOS CI is reached by some ordinary pull requests and not others. So `reach` is one of three values, not a flag: every-pull-request, selected-pull-requests (which must name its condition in reachedWhen) and separate-session. Two surfaces may share a location and differ in reach: config and config-experiment are both repository and CI inspection. macos-native is the selected-pull-requests case: .github/workflows/ci.yml gates swift-macos-arm64 on scripts/ci_scope.py, so a documentation-only pull request never reaches it, while any pull request touching source, scripts or workflows does. The A-level rows were conditional too, and saying otherwise was this map's own worst error. An earlier revision defended one `automated` surface at every-pull-request reach because its portable tests run in the Linux container on any branch; that described a local run, not CI, and CI is what a map of which pull requests reach a surface publishes. At the time the always-running job ran the Python checkers and the scripts/tests suite, and the LabelCore Swift suite and the accelerator checks ran only inside scripts/ci-swift.sh in the gated macOS job. So `automated` is split by executor into automated-preflight, automated-swift and automated-macos. automated-macos carries the same reachedWhen condition as macos-native because the same swift_changed output gates both. automated-swift now reaches every pull request, because .github/workflows/ci.yml runs its executors in the unconditional portable-ubuntu-arm64 job; the split still stands, because it is by executor, and the executors of the other two surfaces did not move. See derivedFrom.portableJob. automated-macos holds the level A rows no portable session can obtain at all: the LabelMac test files M2-AC05 and M3-AC03 bind, under a package that does not build on Linux, and M5-AC12, whose signing-mode default and Developer-ID refusal are decided by scripts/build-local-app.sh, a Darwin-gated shell script that only scripts/ci-swift.sh invokes. Naming the checker that reads a capture is not naming the program that produced it, and grepping for a language finds no executor when the executor is bash. That surface is not macos-native, which is level I: a surface must declare the level its criteria prescribe, so two surfaces may share a host and differ in level exactly as config and config-experiment share a location and differ in reach. See derivedFrom.executorSplit and derivedFrom.macosExecutorSplit for the basis of each row. Nothing here constrains reach by level. An earlier revision of scripts/check_test_surfaces.py refused any level H or R surface that claimed per-pull-request reach, on the reasoning that CI must reach no private printer and no release gate. That rule was removed. A level says what a pass establishes, not whether a pull request may obtain one -- level R describes an installation and distribution lifecycle, not the act of publishing, and a secret-free pull request could exercise an ad-hoc candidate's lifecycle without publishing anything. The rule was therefore the very conflation of the two questions this file exists to separate. The honest basis for such a constraint is a declared effect, such as writing to a device or publishing an artifact, and this map declares no effects. This file records where a criterion CAN be validated and nothing about whether it HAS been. That is docs/ACCEPTANCE-EVIDENCE.json, and a surface here is never evidence there.

automated-preflight.runsOn: the always-running repository-preflight job -- scripts/check_repo.py and the scripts/tests Python suite on the Linux runner -- and any local checkout
automated-preflight.establishes: Committed metadata and schemas, and the portable Python accept/reject rules the repository checkers own: link and JSON validity, milestone document completeness, action pinning and forbidden workflow configuration, the reference-target fields, the native-artifact and signing-mode parsing rules, and the traceability and evidence-record schema.
automated-preflight.doesNotEstablish: Anything the Swift engine computes. A Python unit test of an oracle's own rules is not a run of the encoder that oracle judges, and no native print dialog, installed scheduler or physical output is reachable from here either.

automated-swift.runsOn: the LabelCore Swift suite and scripts/run-accelerator-checks.py: on Linux or macOS locally, and in CI in the unconditional portable-ubuntu-arm64 job on every pull request, and again inside scripts/ci-swift.sh in the swift-macos-arm64 job
automated-swift.establishes: Pure functions, known fixtures, simulated faults and bit-exact encoding as the portable Swift engine actually computes them, cross-checked by the independent ZPL and compression oracles the accelerator suite runs against emitted vectors.
automated-swift.doesNotEstablish: Native print dialog, installed scheduler behaviour or physical output. The portable-ubuntu-arm64 job that makes these rows reachable on every pull request runs the debug configuration only; the release-configuration pass stays inside scripts/ci-swift.sh in swift-macos-arm64, which is gated on the repository-preflight job's swift_changed output, so a pull request that does not select that job obtains no release-configuration result here. Nor does a pass here say anything about the level A rows on automated-macos, whose executors do not run on Linux.

automated-macos.runsOn: scripts/ci-swift.sh on an Apple Silicon macOS host: the LabelMac Swift suite and scripts/build-local-app.sh, and in CI only inside the swift-macos-arm64 job
automated-macos.establishes: The level A claims whose evidence only a macOS host can produce: the LabelMac worker, bitmap-binding and profile-bound job-plan tests, and the signing-mode default and Developer-ID refusal that scripts/build-local-app.sh itself decides before any capture is written.
automated-macos.doesNotEstablish: Anything a portable Linux session can obtain, and anything a noninteractive native run cannot: no print dialog, no installed scheduler, no device and no physical output. Packages/LabelMac does not build on Linux and scripts/build-local-app.sh exits 2 unless uname -s is Darwin, so a portable session reaches none of these rows; nor does a pull request that never ran swift-macos-arm64. A Python test of scripts/check_native_artifacts.py exercises synthetic captures and is not a run of the script that produced a real one.
automated-macos.reachedWhen: the pull request changes a path scripts/ci_scope.py classifies as Swift-affecting

config.runsOn: repository and CI inspection on the pull request under review
config.establishes: Actual repository settings, CI execution, action pins and policy inspection.
config.doesNotEstablish: Product behaviour not covered by executed tests, CI behaviour that only a purpose-built pull request can show, a live repository setting that no committed file records, or anything that happened before the repository existed.

macos-native.establishes: Real Apple frameworks and executables on a recorded Apple Silicon runtime.
macos-native.doesNotEstablish: Application dialogs, an installed scheduler, a retail host, any device, a non-Apple-Silicon runtime, or a performance threshold: the plan treats shared hosted-runner timing as informational only. It also establishes nothing on a pull request that never ran it. swift-macos-arm64 is conditional on the repository-preflight job's swift_changed output, which scripts/ci_scope.py sets from the changed paths, so a pull request touching only Markdown, LICENSE, docs/PROGRESS.json, docs/milestones.json or docs/requirements.json skips this surface entirely. The classifier fails open to testing, so an uncertain diff runs it.
macos-native.reachedWhen: the pull request changes a path scripts/ci_scope.py classifies as Swift-affecting

config-experiment.runsOn: dedicated pull requests built for the experiment, including a contributor-like fork
config-experiment.establishes: CI behaviour that only a purpose-built pull request can show: an intentionally failing check blocking the aggregate, a documentation-only change not stranding required checks, and a fork pull request running the allowed checks without maintainer secrets.
config-experiment.doesNotEstablish: Anything an ordinary pull request shows about itself. The experiment branches are temporary and only the intentional failure is removed afterwards; the observations are recorded, not the branches.

gui.establishes: Required applications, the system print dialog, the extraction editor, accessibility.
gui.doesNotEstablish: Physical output. Earlier attempts failed with cgWindowNotFound; the surface is uncertified.

installed.runsOn: test Mac with an installed scheduler or helper
installed.establishes: Real CUPS queues, held jobs, ownership, the privileged boundary, install and uninstall lifecycle.
installed.doesNotEstablish: Physical output. Requires separate installation authorization.

benchmark.runsOn: the named reference Mac, release build, with a retained baseline commit
benchmark.establishes: Latency, peak memory, output bytes and throughput measured repeatably on one recorded machine with the same fixtures and media, which is what a reviewed threshold can be set against.
benchmark.doesNotEstablish: Anything from shared hosted-runner timing, which the plan and the M2 and M6 specs treat as informational and not a precise performance SLA. Not a physical or mechanical speed.

per-claim.runsOn: one session per advertised claim, in the environment that claim itself names
per-claim.establishes: Exactly the one advertised claim whose own evidence was obtained: an Intel claim by execution on Intel, an IPP claim by exercising its integration path, an extra transport by a session on that transport.
per-claim.doesNotEstablish: Any claim from compilation, from a hosted Apple Silicon run, or from another claim's evidence. There is no single session for this surface. An unexercised claim is withdrawn or marked unavailable, never carried; where a claim additionally needs device observation, that H evidence is recorded separately.

physical.establishes: Observed output, status and finishing on a named device configuration.
physical.doesNotEstablish: Other resolutions, firmware, accessories or the model family; the S1 unit is tear-off with no cutter, so no cut or peel behaviour can be observed on it. Needs explicit consent naming the device and a finite label budget.

accessory.runsOn: an approved accessory target: a printer that actually has the cutter or peeler under test
accessory.establishes: Observed cut policy per label, per batch and at end of job, and peel wait and resume behaviour, on hardware that has the accessory.
accessory.doesNotEstablish: Anything about the S1 tear-off GC420d, which has no cutter and disabled peel behaviour, and nothing the S1 baseline can supply. This is deferred S2 hardware; without it these behaviours stay explicitly unqualified and gate full parity closure.

release.establishes: Exact candidate installation and distribution lifecycle, declared signing mode and provenance.
release.doesNotEstablish: Untested configurations or all future releases. A clean user account is not a clean host.

bootstrap.runsOn: a fresh temporary checkout, plus a separate checkout against an existing repository
bootstrap.establishes: That the documented creation sequence was actually run: a recorded authenticated owner and target repository, and an existing repository's content preserved rather than reset, reinitialised or force-pushed, or its absence established before creation.
bootstrap.doesNotEstablish: Anything an ordinary pull request shows about itself. The pull request under review is made against a repository that already exists, so it cannot observe what was established before creation; the M0 matrix asks for a bootstrap rehearsal in a fresh temporary checkout and a repository-collision check against an existing one, and neither is the pull request being reviewed. Kept separate from repo-settings because the apparatus differs: this is a checkout anyone can make, run once at creation, and observes files rather than settings.

repo-settings.runsOn: an authenticated maintainer inspection of the live repository settings
repo-settings.establishes: The settings the repository holds rather than the files it contains: whether private vulnerability reporting is available, what branch protection is configured, and which permission blocks apply.
repo-settings.doesNotEstablish: Anything a committed file can show. SECURITY.md records the policy a maintainer intends; it is not the setting, and a checker reading it observes a document, not a configuration. Pull request jobs run with a read-only token and cannot read these settings at all, so this needs maintainer authority rather than repository inspection on the pull request under review. Kept separate from bootstrap because the apparatus differs: no checkout is involved, the observation can be repeated at any time, and it requires administrative access a contributor does not have.
